data.narrative:
Oishii, a Series C robotics and manufacturing company founded by Hiroki Koga and Brendan Somerville, has raised $386M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comparable universe of 9 private peers and 1 public company in the robotics and manufacturing sector, including stage-adjacent businesses such as Exotec (Series D, $2.0B), Bedrock Robotics (Series B, $1.8B), and Dexterity (Series B, $1.6B).

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis, using total capital raised as a proxy anchor, applies a 1.7x step-up multiplier typical of Series C advancement, yielding $656M. Peer-median valuation across 7 same-sector comparables at the same or adjacent stage produced a median valuation of $1.6B, with a range spanning $1.0B to $2.0B.

The two methods triangulate to a range of $557M (low) to $1.9B (high), with a median implied valuation of $1.2B. The stage-progression method produces the conservative bound, reflecting capital invested; the peer-median approach anchors the upper range. Key uncertainties include Oishii's relative positioning on unit economics and deployment scale versus the peer cohort, which spans stages B through D and shows considerable spread at $1.0B–$2.0B.
